title: Signature Peer-Reviewed Journal Rating
body:
Signature Peer-Reviewed Journal Rating belongs to the Source Reliability and Authority Ratings collection, which is organised around one clear purpose: to make an AI answer traceable, checkable, and honest about its limits. In the Signature edition, this design is expressed in Manon's own Signature framing: a peer-reviewed journal is rated on editorial review, retraction history, and whether methods and data are stated plainly enough to be checked. The record is written so that a reader with no prior exposure to this method can follow it from start to finish, and so that a reviewer can test each claim in it without taking any step on trust.

How it works. The method begins by naming its inputs in plain language: what is being judged, what evidence is available, and what would count as a successful check. It then applies a stated rule to those inputs, step by step, recording each intermediate result as it goes. Because the rule is stated before the result is computed, a later reader can rerun the same steps and arrive at the same result, or can point to the exact step where a disagreement begins. That rerun property is what separates a method in this collection from an opinion dressed up as a method.

Worked example. In the worked example attached to this record, the demo program computes a concrete result from stated inputs, and the calculation is recorded as: weighted score 0.596 from authority 0.62, methodology 0.55, provenance 0.71, relevance 0.48. The example is illustrative: its numbers are chosen to show the arithmetic clearly, not to describe any real organisation, person, or event. A reader who changes an input can predict how the output should change, and the demo program makes that prediction testable in seconds. If the demo output and the recorded calculation ever disagree, the record is wrong and the demo output governs, because the demo was genuinely executed at build time.

Checks and limits. Every record in this collection carries the same four checks: schema, completeness, consistency, and demo re-execution. The schema check confirms that all required fields are present and correctly typed. The completeness check confirms that the body states method, example, limits, and use. The consistency check confirms that the fields, the calculation, and the demo output agree with each other. The demo re-execution check reruns the demo program and compares its output byte for byte with the stored output. The limits of this method are equally plain: it judges only what its inputs describe, it cannot rescue missing evidence, and it must not be used to launder a guess into a verified fact. This is a Signature original design, written for the Signature ecosystem. It is not a public record and it does not claim to describe any outside system.

Use in the archive. In the wider archive, this record sits on the teaching ladder at the simple tier, so that simpler records introduce the vocabulary, compounded records combine methods, and most-complex records handle disputes, edge cases, and full audits. Its specialist AI can explain the method, run the demo logic on new inputs supplied by the user, and route questions outside its scope to the related databases linked from its page. The record is one step in the march to a million: a small, complete, checkable piece of a much larger system that is built to be used, not merely admired.

authority = 0.62
